  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.

  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.

- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.

- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. name: project-plp-grid-placeholder
description: "PLP still renders through a placeholder SimpleGrid, not the final Zimm grid — card-width symptoms (e.g. size-chip overflow) trace back to this, not to the shared card components"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project

  modified: 2026-09-10T11:14:06.414Z
---

PLP's product grid (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`) still renders via a placeholder
`SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}`, not the finished Zimm-designed grid (4 columns, cards capped
at exactly 288px) that Full History (`ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) and the Rail already use. At a
typical desktop viewport this produces cards roughly ~200px wide — meaningfully narrower than the
~288px the shared product card (and everything inside it, e.g. the size-chip row) is actually
designed against.

**Why:** PLP was explicitly built as a "quick test integration" (SFCC-83/84) to exercise
`ZimmProductCard` on a real page before a dedicated PLP grid component existed — the page's own
code comment already says this. Confirmed concretely 2026-09-10 while investigating a reported
size-chip-group regression: computed PLP's actual available card content width from its own layout
math (sidebar width, gaps, page padding) and showed that six fixed-28px chips (168px minimum, even
at zero gap) already exceed the ~122px of content-box width a ~200px placeholder card leaves after
its own 40px×2 padding. The chip row was never going to fit — not because of a chip-spacing bug,
but because the card itself is too narrow. Marcel confirmed: leave as-is, waiting on the real Zimm
PLP grid implementation; this is a known, already-accepted interim state, not a regression.

**How to apply:** if a future card-content overflow/spacing symptom shows up specifically on PLP
(not on Full History or the Rail, which already use the real grid), check PLP's own card width
first before assuming the shared card/size-chip components are broken — they may be completely
correct and simply not have enough room on PLP's current placeholder grid. The real fix is
building PLP's own final grid (a separate, larger piece of work), not re-touching the shared card
components. See [[project_sfcc55_footer_state]]-style precedent: don't re-diagnose a known,
already-explained gap from scratch.

Two structural gaps found don't belong to this PR and were 13 deliberately kept off its review thread — tracked here instead so they aren't rediscovered cold. 14 15 **`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx`'s tag allow-list has no ``.** Any hyperlink inside 16 SFCC-sourced rich text (AP21 `environmentalNotes`, BM site-pref `environmentalMessage`, and 17 presumably any other field routed through `ZimmProductDescription`) gets silently unwrapped to 18 plain unclickable text — confirmed live, no security implication (attributes never reach 19 `createElement`), just a fidelity gap. First real case that needed it was SFCC-266's "Packaging" 20 link (Figma shows it underlined; Jira SFCC-765 comment 14498 authors it as a real link). Whoever 21 picks this up next should extend `ALLOWED_TAGS` with `'a'` plus `href`/`target` attribute 22 handling — it's shared code, not scoped to one PR. 23 **Why it matters:** will resurface on any future ticket that routes a real link through this 24 parser, not just SFCC-266. 25 **How to apply:** flag it the moment a new ticket's content needs a working link; don't assume 26 it already works because the tag renders. 27 28 **`ZimmProductDescription`'s own recipe (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts`) owns paragraph 29 spacing (currently 20px, explicitly flagged there as provisional/pending UI-designer sign-off), 30 but `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx` overrides it to 64px from outside via a `sx` selector 31 reaching into the atom's internal markup.** Confirmed live: it's also a no-op whenever the 32 content renders as a single text run (no siblings for `* + *` to select), which is the likely 33 case for the BM fallback message and possibly for AP21 notes too (SFCC-26's sample value reads 34 as plain/markdown text, not `

`-tagged HTML) — unconfirmed end-to-end, no product in the test 35 catalog currently has real `environmentalNotes` populated to check. 36 **Why it matters:** the correct fix is a variant on `ZimmProductDescription`'s own recipe, not 37 another consumer-side override — see [[project_styling_layer_boundary]] for the same class of 38 mistake elsewhere in this codebase. 39 **How to apply:** next time this recipe's spacing value comes up for actual designer sign-off, 40 resolve both the 20px-vs-64px question and this override in the same pass. 41 42 **Squad-ownership docs contradict the real gate.** `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `squadB.md` 43 both claim `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` and `product-list/` as Squad A territory. 44 CODEOWNERS actually routes both to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` — confirmed this is what's really 45 enforced (explains why GitHub auto-requested Squad B review on a PR whose own body table claimed 46 Squad A ownership). Nobody has reconciled this; flagged to Marcel, no ticket raised yet. 47 **Why it matters:** CODEOWNERS is what actually gates merges, so nothing is unsafe, but the two 48 draft docs will keep misdirecting whoever reads them for "who do I notify" purposes. 49 **How to apply:** don't trust squadA.md/squadB.md for `product-detail/`/`product-list/` 50 ownership without cross-checking CODEOWNERS first. 51 52 **Locale-key mismatch, unresolved.** Jira SFCC-266/SFCC-765 and the SFCC-side PR 53 (zimmermann-sfcc#39) describe the BM site preference as seeded with `en_FR`/`fr_FR`. This repo's 54 `config/sites.overlay.js` routes `/en-eu/` → locale `en-GB`, `/fr-eu/` → locale `fr`. The feature 55 empirically still works correctly on the live PR preview for both routes, so either the SFCC-side 56 docs are stale or there's a normalization step invisible from this repo. Not verified either way. 57 **Why it matters:** if it's really a mismatch and not normalization, it's fragile — a future BM 58 preferences change matching the *documented* locale keys instead of the *real* ones could 59 silently break the gate. 60 **How to apply:** worth a two-minute confirmation with Integration before it's built on top of 61 again; don't assume either side is correct. 62

Supersedes an earlier note of mine that called this unsettled and said "build flat, don't create
`atoms/`". **That was wrong** — it came from a 19 Aug analysis that was superseded later in the
same session once the decision landed.

**Placement — decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live at:
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx`
(today: `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` as atoms;
`zimmInputAction` as the one molecule; no organisms yet).

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own, don't generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing |
|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab — must match upstream's import path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase — Zimmermann-authored, the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase — mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note also the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**Tier — by what the component's own template renders**, not visual size. Atom = renders no other
component; Molecule = only atoms; Organism = ≥1 molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count
(`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom), and slotted children don't count. When porting from the
F2R library the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it rather than re-deriving,
and add `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` in the JSDoc.

**Styling surface — decided: a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class,
not co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is
the bridge — native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. **Register the
recipe in `theme/components/index.ts` or destructuring throws at runtime.** F2R `.styles.ts` files
using `.zimm-*` classes are a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and good raw material — *convert
them to a recipe, don't copy the pattern*; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning against co-located CSS is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`,
which is **derived output at the bottom of the token pipeline**. Author there and you lose
`textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the
theme drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

**Planning fact:** `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven** directories
(`_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`).
`product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`, `list-menu`,
`drawer-menu`, `seo` are all still `Origin = Base` despite being referenced throughout
`.claude/rules/`. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example
not to exist yet.

**Why:** getting this wrong adds a fifth competing structure, and my own stale version of it would
have sent a future build in the opposite direction from the agreed one.

**How to apply:** source is Marcel's `~/Dev/fedBuild-manual.md` §2–§3 — **local-only, never
cite it in a PR, commit or code comment** ([[feedback-local-only-docs]]). Cite `conventions.md` /

13	deliberately **not** registered. Consequences, both measured during SFCC-55 (session 652997c6):
14

16	  `theme.sizes`, so a bare key falls through to Chakra's defaults — measured blow-up range

18	  **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
19	- **Typography props** have the same twin: `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
20	  intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all.
21	
22	**Always use the CSS var on those props** — `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`.
23	Spacing props (`margin`/`padding`/`gap`) are fine with bare keys.
24	
25	Two related traps from the same work: Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value, so
26	`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser (use axis props); and a
27	shorthand declared *after* a longhand resets it (`padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` — use
28	`paddingInline`).

---
name: project-chakra-scale-registration
description: Only space/colors/fonts/borderWidths/breakpoints/textStyles are registered in the Chakra theme — sizes, fontSizes, lineHeights and letterSpacings are NOT, so bare token keys on those props silently misresolve
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f
  modified: 2026-08-22T02:20:00.000Z
---

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only**
(`space: spacing`, line 56). `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are
deliberately **not** registered. Consequences, both measured during SFCC-55 (session 652997c6):

- **Sizing props** (`width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height`) resolve through
  `theme.sizes`, so a bare key falls through to Chakra's defaults — measured blow-up range
  **8×–112×** (`width: 'xl'` rendered footer contact icons at **576px**). Worse, `s`/`m`/`l` are
  **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
- **Typography props** have the same twin: `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
  intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Always use the CSS var on those props** — `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`.
Spacing props (`margin`/`padding`/`gap`) are fine with bare keys.

Two related traps from the same work: Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value, so
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser (use axis props); and a
shorthand declared *after* a longhand resets it (`padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` — use
`paddingInline`).

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has
`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing. Pre-existing, outside the footer scope, still there as of
2026-08-22.

**Why:** these fail silently — no error, no warning, just wrong or absent CSS. The 576px icon
bug destroyed the entire footer layout before the cause was found.

**How to apply:** `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards the first two cases (bare key on a sizing prop,
bare key in a compound shorthand) and is mutation-verified — run it after touching any recipe.
`theme/index.ts`'s own header comment lists what is and isn't registered.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue_development_info
entries.description:
Get development information (PRs, commits, branches) linked to a Jira issue.

This retrieves the development panel information that shows linked
pull requests, branches, and commits from connected source control systems
like Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitLab.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: The Jira issue key.
    application_type: Optional filter by source control type.
    data_type: Optional filter by data type (pullrequest, branch, etc.).

Returns:
    JSON string with development information including:
    - pullRequests: List of linked pull requests with status, author, reviewers
    - branches: List of linked branches
    - commits: List of linked commits
    - repositories: List of repositories involved

application_type.description: (Optional) Filter by application type. Examples: 'stash' (Bitbucket Server), 'bitbucket', 'github', 'gitlab'

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

connection.message: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly. For more information, pass `verbose: true` in the second argument to fetch()

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_design_context
entries.description:
Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. 

IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. 

NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions.

Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

1	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
2	import { DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT } from 'app/theme/components/zimmDrawerShared';
3	
4	// Figma's actual named drawer sizes (SFCC-898) — five named sizes, not the three/four this
5	// file previously guessed at. Each name below matches Figma's own naming exactly, so there's
6	// no re-deriving which number belongs to which concept next time this file is touched:
7	//
8	//   Desktop Large — 50%  — Product Details, Filters (desktop width)
9	//   Tablet        — 80%  — Product Details, Filters (tablet width)
10	//   Desktop Small — 25%  — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront,
11	//                           Cookies, Login
12	//   X-Large       — 82%  — Cart (not yet built as a drawer — see the `xLarge` variant below)
13	//   Mobile        — unchanged, the baseStyle treatment every variant collapses to below `md`.
14	//
15	// An earlier revision of this file measured 82% off a Figma frame annotated "Tablet = 82% of
16	// screen" and used it as `small`'s (now `tablet`'s) value — that frame's annotation was wrong
17	// (or superseded): 82% is actually X-Large's value (Cart), a completely different drawer this
18	// codebase hasn't built yet, and Tablet is genuinely 80%. Corrected once confirmed directly
19	// against the list above, not another single frame's own label.
20	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
21	const WIDTH_TABLET = '80%';
22	// The original width set when this drawer shell was first built (2026-08-27) — matches Figma's
23	// "Desktop Small" exactly. Used by every viewport-independent narrow utility drawer (Find in
24	// Boutique today; Notify Me/Wishlist/Regional Storefront/Cookies/Login once those exist).
25	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';
26	// Cart isn't built as a drawer yet (confirmed: it's a full page today) — this constant and the
27	// `xLarge` variant below exist so the real Figma value is already in place, under the right
28	// name, whenever that work starts, rather than needing this same "which number is this?"
29	// investigation again.
30	const WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%';
31	
32	// Mobile deliberately leaves a strip of backdrop visible below the panel (SFCC-736 AC 9,
33	// PO-approved 2026-08-21 — "so a user can easily navigate out"). Re-measured against node
34	// 40002218:42903 (SFCC-898): overlay 956px tall, panel 898px tall — exactly 58px. No named
35	// spacing scale step lands on 58px, so this is a provisional raw value pending a foundation
36	// token, same as the other pending constants in this file.
37	const MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP = '3.625rem'; // 58px
38	
39	// Close-button inset, measured from the pdp/drawer header frames. `tablet`/`small`/`xLarge`/
40	// `mobile` all share the same measured inset (32px/40px) at every width — only `large` switches
41	// to the wider 48px/64px inset, at/above the tablet breakpoint. Below that breakpoint `large`'s
42	// own override doesn't apply either, and the baseStyle inset is used instead, which is also how
43	// the whole drawer collapses to the mobile treatment on a narrow viewport regardless of `size`.
44	const INSET_COMPACT = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)' };
45	const INSET_LARGE = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)' };
46	
47	// Header constants — from Figma drawer/header frame measurements.
48	// Compact horizontal inset (small/mobile): px=32px. Large desktop: px=64px.
49	// Small desktop header uses py=24px. Large desktop: container height=120px (row centred).
50	// Mobile base: container height=72px.
51	const HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'; // 32px
52	const HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)'; // 64px
53	const HEADER_PADDING_Y = 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'; // 24px — small desktop py
54	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed container heights with no --zimm-scale equivalents at these values.
55	const HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE = '120px';
56	const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '72px';
57	
58	export const ZimmDrawer = {
59	  parts: ['overlay', 'content', 'closeButton', 'header', 'headerTitle'],
60	  baseStyle: {
61	    // Explicit position/inset rather than relying on Chakra's own built-in `Drawer` overlay
62	    // styling — confirmed via inspection that it doesn't apply (renders `position: static`,
63	    // zero size) when the `<Drawer>` isn't given Chakra's own `size` prop, which this component
64	    // deliberately omits (see maxWidth note below). Owning it here avoids depending on that.
65	    overlay: {
66	      position: 'fixed',
67	      inset: 0,
68	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)',
69	      zIndex: 'overlay',
70	    },
71	    content: {
72	      // Chakra's own <DrawerContent> baked in a default white background
73	      // (@chakra-ui/theme's modal.js `baseStyleDialog`: `bg: colors.white`) that this recipe
74	      // never needed to set itself while that component was still in use — now that
75	      // ZimmDrawer hand-rolls its own content element (see index.tsx's file-level comment),
76	      // nothing supplies one unless it's set here. Matches Figma's pdp/drawer panel background
77	      // (bg-[var(--brand/color/palette/white,white)]) — --zimm-color-bg-07 resolves to the
78	      // same grey.white value (SFCC-898 — the panel briefly had no background at all).
79	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-07)',
80	      width: '100%',
81	      // Matches `width` at every step below — Chakra's own `Drawer` theme defaults to
82	      // `size="xs"` (maxW 20rem) when no `size` prop is passed to `<Drawer>` (deliberate: its
83	      // fixed size scale has no 50%/25% steps), and that default `maxW` otherwise still caps
84	      // our own `width` override since we never reset it.
85	      maxWidth: '100%',
86	      // Mobile positioning: override index.tsx's hardcoded `right: 0` to allow `left: 0; width: 100%`
87	      // full-width layout. With both `left: 0; right: 0;` on mobile, the drawer stretches
88	      // properly from edge to edge. Without this override, `right: 0; width: 100%` alone (on
89	      // position:fixed) spans from -100% (off left) to 0 (right), causing the pale left stripe.
90	      // Audited 2026-09-16 — contentStyles spread AFTER the hardcoded props in index.tsx,
91	      // so these overrides take effect.
92	      left: 0,
93	      right: 'auto',
94	      // A `height` reduction, not a `bottom` offset — Chakra's own Slide transition (see
95	      // @chakra-ui/transition's slide.js `placement: 'right'` case) pins the sliding wrapper
96	      // with `position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0`, a definite height. `bottom` on
97	      // this `position: relative` DrawerContent just shifts the box within that instead of
98	      // reliably opening a gap (SFCC-898 — mobile bottom gap wasn't rendering at all); a
99	      // percentage `height` resolves cleanly against that definite-height ancestor instead.
100	      height: `calc(100% - ${MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP})`,
101	      // Header stays fixed; only the content area (ZimmPdpDrawer's own `content` part) scrolls —
102	      // AC 10, "content area scrolls independently without the tab header scrolling".
103	      display: 'flex',
104	      flexDirection: 'column',
105	      overflow: 'hidden',
106	    },
107	    // Was missing `position: absolute` since this component's original commit — the
108	    // top/right insets below were silently no-ops (closeButton rendered as a normal in-flow
109	    // block instead of overlaying the header's corner), which is the root cause of SFCC-898's
110	    // close-button-misaligned-with-tabs defect across every breakpoint.
111	    //
112	    // height/display/alignItems/justifyContent: matches zimmTabs.css.ts's `menu.minHeight`
113	    // (DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT, zimmDrawerShared.ts) and centers the icon inside it — the
114	    // close icon's own intrinsic size doesn't equal the tab row's real rendered height, so
115	    // matching only `top` between the two (as before) left their vertical centers slightly
116	    // offset (SFCC-898, mobile). Only applies to the floating close button (no `title` passed) —
117	    // the inline title-row close button below is a normal flex child, not absolutely positioned.
118	    closeButton: {
119	      position: 'absolute',
120	      ...INSET_COMPACT,
121	      height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
122	      display: 'flex',
123	      alignItems: 'center',
124	      justifyContent: 'center',
125	    },
126	    // Drawer header — title (flex-1, left) + close button (right).
127	    // baseStyle applies the mobile/compact treatment: px=32px, container h=72px centred.
128	    header: {
129	      display: 'flex',
130	      alignItems: 'center',
131	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
132	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
133	      paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X,
134	      paddingBlock: 0,
135	      minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
136	      flexShrink: 0,
137	    },
138	    headerTitle: {
139	      flex: '1 0 0',
140	      minWidth: 0,
141	      overflow: 'hidden',
142	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
143	    },
144	  },
145	  variants: {
146	    large: {
147	      content: {
148	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
149	          width: WIDTH_LARGE,
150	          maxWidth: WIDTH_LARGE,
151	          height: '100%',
152	          // Override baseStyle's mobile `left: 0; right: 'auto'` to restore right-aligned positioning.
153	          left: 'auto',
154	          right: 0,
155	        },
156	      },
157	      closeButton: {
158	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: INSET_LARGE,
159	      },
160	      header: {
161	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
162	          paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X,
163	          minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE,
164	        },
165	      },
166	    },
167	    // Figma's "Tablet" size — the tablet-range step for Product Details/Filters, which
168	    // graduates to `large` (Desktop Large) at the desktop breakpoint via the caller's own
169	    // useBreakpointValue (ZimmPdpDrawer never selects this variant itself).
170	    tablet: {
171	      content: {
172	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
173	          width: WIDTH_TABLET,
174	          maxWidth: WIDTH_TABLET,
175	          height: '100%',
176	          left: 'auto',
177	          right: 0,
178	        },
179	      },
180	    },
181	    // Figma's "Desktop Small" — always narrow, at every width above the mobile collapse. No

184	    small: {

187	          width: WIDTH_SMALL,
188	          maxWidth: WIDTH_SMALL,
189	          height: '100%',
190	          left: 'auto',
191	          right: 0,
192	        },
193	      },
194	    },
195	    // Figma's "X-Large" (Cart) — not consumed anywhere yet (Cart is a full page today, not a

197	    xLarge: {
198	      content: {

200	          width: WIDTH_XLARGE,
201	          maxWidth: WIDTH_XLARGE,
202	          height: '100%',
203	          left: 'auto',
204	          right: 0,
205	        },
206	      },

210	          paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
211	        },
212	      },
213	    },
214	    // No override — the baseStyle above already is the mobile treatment.
215	    mobile: {},

input.prompt:
You are reviewing PR #117 in the zimmermann-pwa repo (feat(plp): SFCC-847 add filter drawer with responsive chip selection). This is a large PR (32 files, +2678/-264) implementing a PLP filter drawer. I (the lead reviewer) have already established ground truth on Jira/Figma/process; your job is to test the CODE across multiple angles and report findings, not to fix anything.

## How to get the diff
Base SHA `71025f182af083bff423ead28490084e3efb4044` (develop), head SHA `15dbd98e0aa1deab60bbb0ffebac57da87855e5d` (PR branch). A worktree already exists at `/tmp/claude-501/pr117-review` — it is currently checked out at the BASE commit (I was using it for gate comparisons). Run `git -C /tmp/claude-501/pr117-review checkout 15dbd98e0aa1deab60bbb0ffebac57da87855e5d` first to get back to head before reading any files there, or just use `git -C /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa diff 71025f182af083bff423ead28490084e3efb4044..15dbd98e0aa1deab60bbb0ffebac57da87855e5d` from the main repo (both SHAs are already fetched as local refs there). Don't mutate the worktree's checked-out ref and leave it elsewhere without noting it in your report.

## Ticket scope (for context, not yours to adjudicate — I own the scope verdict separately)
SFCC-847 ("drawer/content/filters") explicitly scopes ITSELF to: the accordion shell + CLEAR/APPLY button *rendering* only. Its own description and comments explicitly say: the drawer shell/overlay/close trigger belong to SFCC-736 (separate, already Done/In SIT); "the filter facet content rendered inside each accordion (radio buttons, colour swatches, size options etc.)" and "CLEAR and APPLY button *behaviour* (resetting selections and applying filters to the product grid)" are explicitly SFCC-108's scope, not SFCC-847's (confirmed in Jira comments where AC4/AC5/AC9/AC10 were deliberately moved out of SFCC-847 to SFCC-108). SFCC-108 itself is currently status "Blocked", depending on SFCC-104 (BM facet configuration) which is still "Code Review" (not done). I already know the PR implements far more than SFCC-847's stated shell/rendering-only scope (real facet checkbox/size logic, a 153-line `useFilterDrawerState` hook with real state management, CLEAR ALL behavior). Do NOT re-litigate this scope question — just flag anything you find that's relevant to it as you go; I'm covering the scope verdict myself via a separate check.

## What I've already confirmed myself (don't re-derive, but feel free to double check anything that seems off)
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` and `zimmTokens.ts` (Tier 1, design-system) are touched — adds one new `border.tertiary` alias (`#dddddd`), justified with a comment tracing it to a real Figma alias with no primitive equivalent. Looks legitimate but is a Tier 1 file regardless.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/` (shared shell, used by PDP's already-Done/In-SIT drawer AND wishlist auth AND now this new filters drawer) had its scroll-lock `useEffect` (module-level counter, added for SFCC-926) DELETED entirely, and `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` (2 tests covering baseStyle/mobile-variant content height) was deleted wholesale with no replacement. The base/mobile height and left/right positioning logic was also restructured (baseStyle now always applies `left:0;right:auto;height:calc(100% - 58px)`, with each of large/tablet/small/xLarge variants explicitly resetting `left:auto;right:0` only inside a `@media (min-width:md)` block — meaning below the md breakpoint, EVERY drawer instance app-wide, including PDP's which explicitly requests `size="mobile"` via `useBreakpointValue({base:'mobile',...})`, now gets the new baseStyle treatment). I could not settle in a live browser whether this is a real visible regression for PDP/wishlist-auth (the PR's own live MRT preview 404s on every category/PLP page I tried, traced to a genuine backend category-not-found from `useCategory`, unrelated to app code — so I couldn't visually check the filter drawer OR PDP live). Please look hard at this specific area: is there a real visible regression risk for PDP's mobile drawer or the wishlist auth drawer from this restructuring? Is the deleted test file's coverage genuinely gone with nothing replacing it? A new `hasOverlay` prop was added (defaults true) and is used with `hasOverlay={false}` only by the new filters drawer at `product-list/index.tsx:1172` — I've independently confirmed via the actual Figma frame ("PLP New all - Filters open - Collapsed - Desktop", file wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm node 40003890:151730) that there's no dimming scrim in the design, so `hasOverlay={false}` for filters is correct — don't re-flag that part.
- Gate numbers I measured myself (unverified by you — re-run if a finding depends on one): head tsc passes (exit 0), head lint has 883 problems/824 errors but nearly all are pre-existing prettier drift in unrelated files (e.g. `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts` — not touched by this PR at all) — I have NOT yet fully diffed lint counts against base, flag if you spot anything in the PR's OWN new/touched files beyond what I already found: `product-list/index.tsx` has several `@typescript-eslint/restrict-template-expressions` warnings and 2 unused-var warnings (`_unusedIsLoading`, `_unusedStaticContext`), `useFilterDrawerState.ts` has 2 unused-var warnings (`_removed` x2). Head vitest: 1208 tests pass across 83 files (includes the whole repo, not just this PR). Head audit:tokens: exactly 3 unacknowledged violations, and I confirmed none of the 3 offending files (`footer/footer.css.ts`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`) are touched by this PR — so this PR adds zero new unacknowledged token violations (please spot-check this conclusion rather than trust it blindly).

## Angles to cover (split across your own sub-dispatches as you see fit given the size)
1. **Correctness & regression** — `useFilterDrawerState.ts` (153 lines) + its test (168 lines): chip-pagination math (3 desktop / 2 "lg" / 1 mobile per the PR description), the CLEAR ALL action that "navigates to parent category for category chips", the buffered-vs-applied filter selection state. Does the logic hold up, including edge cases (zero results, all filters cleared, rapid toggle)?
2. **Conventions & tier ownership** — check every new/touched file against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `components.md`, `overrideStyling.md`, `css.md`, `typescript.md` (no bare Chakra token keys on sizing/typography props — see the project's own known Chakra-scale-registration trap: only `space`/`colors`/`fonts`/`borderWidths`/`breakpoints`/`textStyles` are registered, `sizes`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are NOT, so a bare key there silently misresolves or drops — check zimmAccordion, zimmSelectedChip, zimmSizeRefinements, zimmCheckboxRefinements, zimmFiltersDrawerContent specifically for this). Check Storybook/test existence per testing.md for every new component. Check `.claude/registry/*.md` diffs are consistent with the actual new components (not stale/wrong).
3. **Contract fidelity** — `ZimmButton`'s new discriminated-union toggle semantics (role/aria-checked). Does every EXISTING (pre-PR) call site of ZimmButton across the whole repo still type-check and behave correctly under the new discriminated union, or does this narrow the type in a way that could break other call sites? Is the toggle semantics implementation (role="checkbox"/aria-checked, or whatever it actually does) correct per WAI-ARIA for a checkbox-like toggle button?
4. **Failure modes & security** — facet/refinement data: confirm it's genuinely sourced from live `productSearchResult.refinements` (SDK), not hardcoded — the PR's own comment claims "the earlier hardcodedFilterFacets placeholder has been removed." Given SFCC-104 (BM facet config) is NOT done yet, what happens when refinements come back sparse/malformed/empty from the real API — does the UI degrade gracefully or crash/misrender? Check `overrides/app/utils/refinementValues.ts` (11 lines) for correctness.
5. **Accessibility** — `zimmCheckboxRefinements`, `zimmSizeRefinements`, `zimmAccordion`, `zimmSelectedChip` against `.claude/rules/components.md`'s JSX accessibility rules (img alt, IconButton aria-label, non-native-interactive onClick needs role+tabIndex+onKeyDown). The ticket explicitly asks for "proper screen-reader announcements" on toggle refinements — verify aria-checked/role are wired correctly end to end, not just declared in the type.

Report back with concrete file:line findings, each one already classified as in-scope-defect / out-of-scope / nitpick, and CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE per your own verification. I will run these through my own adjudication and a separate findings-verification pass before anything is posted — so err on the side of flagging anything real rather than pre-filtering for me.

**SFCC-847 ("drawer/content/filters", status: Tech design / To Do)** — full description: "As a Developer, I want a drawer/content/filters component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that shoppers can view, select, and apply product filters from a slide-out drawer on PLP and search results pages. Component list: drawer/filters (panel, variants: Category-PLP-All, Category-PLP-Dresses, Selected, Colour, Size, Availability, Material, Sleeve Length), Accordion (one per facet group, expanded/collapsed, only one open at a time), Button-group (CLEAR secondary + APPLY primary, layout=Inline). Jira comments on this ticket explicitly moved AC4/AC5 ("validate functionality when an option is selected") and AC9/AC10 ("CLEAR/APPLY *behaviour* on click") OUT of SFCC-847 and into SFCC-108, leaving only AC11 ("button *rendering*") in SFCC-847. The ticket's very last comment (posted minutes before this PR opened) is Jira automation auto-rejecting a Definition-of-Ready checklist attempt to advance the ticket, moving it back to To Do.

**SFCC-108 ("Search Results – Filters & Facets UI Component", status: Blocked, depends on SFCC-104 which is still Code Review)** — "This story covers the PWA build of the filter panel, consuming facet configuration from BM. It includes rendering of global and category-level facets, multi-select logic within and across facets, colour swatch display, applied filter labels with individual and clear-all removal, and availability filter display... CLEAR and APPLY button behaviour (resetting selections and applying filters to the product grid) is owned by this story. The drawer shell and accordion structure are covered in SFCC-847."

**SFCC-736 ("pdp/drawer", status: In SIT / Done)** — the shared drawer SHELL component (ZimmDrawer) — "responsible for the drawer shell only — the slide-in panel, overlay backdrop, close button... It does not own the content rendered within each tab."

The PR's own description claims: "Adds ZimmFiltersDrawerContent organism (accordion + footer buttons) and refactors PLP filter state into a custom hook (useFilterDrawerState). Implements responsive selected-chip pagination... with arrow controls and CLEAR ALL action that navigates to parent category for category chips. Extends ZimmButton with toggle semantics... used by size and checkbox refinements for proper screen-reader announcements." It also modifies the shared `ZimmDrawer` shell itself (SFCC-736's component, already Done/In SIT) and adds new atoms `zimmCheckboxRefinements`/`zimmSizeRefinements` (facet content rendering) plus a 153-line `useFilterDrawerState` hook with real multi-select/apply/clear state management and a 168-line test for it.

Judge: does the actual diff match SFCC-847's own stated (shell + rendering-only) scope, or does it substantively deliver SFCC-108's scope (facet content rendering, multi-select logic, CLEAR/APPLY *behaviour*) and touch SFCC-736's already-shipped territory?
