CORRECTION to my brief — important, please apply before you go further.

I gave you base SHA 71025f182af083bff423ead28490084e3efb4044 (develop's current tip) as the diff base. That was wrong. This PR's branch is actually 41 commits BEHIND develop's current tip and was never rebased — the TRUE merge-base is a different, older commit: 2510cea566d52fae7f430cfc8f3fc983e56d7266.

Please redo any diffing with: `git diff 2510cea566d52fae7f430cfc8f3fc983e56d7266..15dbd98e0aa1deab60bbb0ffebac57da87855e5d`

This matters a lot for two things I told you that turn out to be FALSE — please drop/ignore them entirely:

1. I claimed the PR deletes `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` wholesale and removes the SFCC-926 scroll-lock `useEffect` from `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`. **This is wrong.** Against the correct merge-base, the PR does NOT touch the scroll-lock code or delete that test file at all — those apparent "changes" were purely an artifact of comparing against develop's stale-relative-to-this-branch tip (something else, unrelated to this PR, added/changed that on develop after this branch diverged). Please do not report anything about scroll-lock removal or that test deletion — it isn't real.

2. The TRUE zimmDrawer diff (verified by me against the correct merge-base) is much narrower than what a develop-tip diff would show: it only (a) adds a `hasOverlay` prop (defaults true, used `false` only by the new filters drawer — I've independently confirmed via the actual Figma frame that no dimming scrim is designed for the filters drawer, so this part is correct, not a defect) and (b) adds `left: 0; right: 'auto'` to `ZimmDrawer`'s baseStyle.content, with the `large`/`tablet`/`small`/`xLarge` named variants explicitly resetting back to `left:'auto';right:0` inside their own `@media (min-width: md)` blocks — but the `mobile` named variant gets no such reset. Since PDP (`product-detail/index.tsx`) explicitly requests `size="mobile"` via `useBreakpointValue({base:'mobile', md:'tablet', xl:'large'})`, this is a PLAUSIBLE (not confirmed by me — I could not verify live, see below) regression risk: PDP's mobile-viewport drawer may flip from right-anchored to left-anchored. The PR's own code comment claims a real "pale left stripe" bug was observed and fixed by this change, which I can't fully evaluate via static reading alone (whether `width:100%` in that flex/inset:0 context is truly viewport-relative or something larger). If you can reason through the actual CSS cascade/flex-parent behavior here, or find any way to check it, that would help settle this properly — otherwise report it as plausible-not-confirmed, same as I have it.

Other than those two corrections, everything else I told you (the theme/foundation Tier 1 touch, the gate numbers, the Jira scope context) still stands as I described it. Sorry for the churn — I caught this by re-deriving the merge-base myself right after dispatching you and wanted to correct it before it propagated into a false finding.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

files, see note below). True scope = 32 files, matches `gh pr view --json files` exactly.

---

1. **[CONFIRMED] SFCC-847 is not ready for development.** Status "Tech design" (To Do category).
   Its own last comment (2026-09-16 11:12, ~1hr before this PR opened) is Jira automation
   auto-rejecting a Definition-of-Ready checklist attempt and moving the ticket back. State: not posted (process fact for Marcel, not a PR comment).

2. **[CONFIRMED] Scope overlap with SFCC-108 (Blocked, depends on SFCC-104 which is Code Review,
   not done).** SFCC-847's own description/comments explicitly exclude facet content rendering
   (checkboxes, colour swatches, size options) and CLEAR/APPLY *behaviour* — both explicitly
   assigned to SFCC-108. This PR implements both anyway (zimmCheckboxRefinements,
   zimmSizeRefinements with real toggle logic, useFilterDrawerState with real apply/clear state).
   Sent to zm-orchestrator for formal scope verdict (pending).

3. **[CONFIRMED] Branch is 41 commits behind develop, never rebased — explains mergeable=CONFLICTING.**
   Not itself a code defect, but means this PR cannot merge as-is regardless of review outcome.

4. **[RETRACTED — do not use] ZimmDrawer scroll-lock removal / zimmDrawer.css.test.ts deletion /
   package.json Tier 1 touch / webpack.config.js deletion.** All four were artifacts of diffing
   PR-head against develop's CURRENT tip instead of the true merge-base. None are real. Corrected
   mid-session; zm-tester and zm-orchestrator were both re-briefed with the correct merge-base.

5. **[CONFIRMED] CodeRabbit has not actually reviewed this PR** — 0 reviews via API, only the
   auto-summary comment, which itself states the author (@bryanian09) has no CodeRabbit seat
   ("Request again after 2026-09-23"). No CodeRabbit input exists to cross-check findings against
   for this PR, unlike prior reviews. Worth asking whether the author ran the required local
   `cr review --light --base develop` per AGENTS.md's Coding Task Workflow step 4 — can't verify
   from the PR alone.

## Code findings (mine, verified against the correct merge-base)

6. **[CONFIRMED] Tier 1 file touched:** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` +
   `zimmTokens.ts` — adds one new alias `border.tertiary: '#dddddd'`. Well-justified inline
   (traces to a real Figma alias with no primitive equivalent, consumed by the new accordion
   divider). Legitimate-looking change, but still Tier 1 — needs the Tier 1 approval process
   (AGENTS.md's verified-session exception or named-owner approval) regardless of quality.

7. **[CONFIRMED, design-fidelity check PASSED — not a defect] `hasOverlay={false}` on the new
   filters drawer.** Verified against the actual Figma frame ("PLP New all - Filters open -
   Collapsed - Desktop", file wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm node 40003890:151730, via screenshot) — no
   dimming scrim in the design. The implementation choice is correct.

8. **[PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed live] `ZimmDrawer` baseStyle.content gains unconditional
   `left:0; right:'auto'`** (previously absent — position was governed solely by a hardcoded
   `right:0` in index.tsx's `MotionChakraDiv`). The four *named* size variants (large/tablet/
   small/xLarge) explicitly reset back to `left:'auto';right:0`, but only inside their own
   `@media (min-width: md)` block. The `mobile` named variant has no such reset, and none of the
   four resets apply below the md breakpoint regardless of which size was requested. PDP
   (`product-detail/index.tsx:848`) explicitly requests `size="mobile"` via `useBreakpointValue`
   at narrow viewports. This is a real, confirmed code change (verified against the correct
   merge-base) to a shared component also used by PDP's already-Done/In-SIT drawer and the
   wishlist-auth drawer. Whether it's visually different in practice is UNCONFIRMED — I could not
   verify live: this PR's own MRT preview (https://zimmermann-pr-f847-d63140d1.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com)
   404s ("Category Not Found", a genuine backend 404 from `useCategory`) on every category/PLP
   page I tried (/clothing/dresses, /new), so I could not load the filter drawer OR a PDP page to
   check this live. The PR's own code comment claims a real "pale left stripe" bug was observed
   and fixed by this change (dated "Audited 2026-09-16") — plausible, but I can't fully resolve
   the CSS cascade by static reading alone. Needs a live check by whoever has a working preview.
   State: not posted.

## Gate comparison (base = true merge-base, head = PR)

| Gate | Base | Head | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| tsc --noEmit | pass (0) | pass (0) | no regression |
| lint | 950 problems (894 err/56 warn) | 883 problems (824 err/59 warn) | net improvement; +3 new warnings are the PR's own 4 unused-var warnings (`_unusedIsLoading`, `_unusedStaticContext` in product-list/index.tsx; `_removed` x2 in useFilterDrawerState.ts) minus some offsetting fixed errors elsewhere |
| vitest | 1229 passed (83 files) | 1208 passed (83 files) | **net -21 tests despite 7 new test files added — needs explanation, see below** |
| audit:tokens | 3 unacknowledged (same 3 files) | 3 unacknowledged (same 3 files) | identical set, none in PR's own files — no regression |

**Open question, not yet resolved:** vitest test count dropped net -21 despite this PR adding 7
new test files (zimmAccordion, zimmCheckboxRefinements, zimmSelectedChip, zimmSizeRefinements,
zimmFiltersDrawerContent, useFilterDrawerState, refinementValues — collectively should add
hundreds of cases going by their line counts). File count is identical at 83 in both runs, so
something removed test files/cases roughly matching what was added, net negative. Given the
confirmed 32-file true scope, the only plausible removed-coverage candidate left in-scope is
whatever `partials/size-refinements.tsx`'s own tests covered before its removal (PR description:
"removes the orphaned partials/size-refinements.tsx override") — need to confirm that file had a
test and whether its case count explains the gap, or whether this is actually normal variance
(e.g. a flaky/conditional test count) — not yet settled.

## Dispatched, pending

- zm-tester (background) — correctness/regression, conventions/tier, contract fidelity (ZimmButton
  discriminated union), failure modes/security (real vs hardcoded facet data), accessibility.
  Re-briefed with correct merge-base mid-flight.
- zm-orchestrator (background) — formal scope verdict vs SFCC-847/108/736. Re-briefed with correct
  merge-base mid-flight.

[]`) but not against `[]` — an empty array renders as an empty `<Stack>`/`<Flex>` with zero children, no "no options available" messaging. **File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmCheckboxRefinements/index.tsx:98`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeRefinements/index.tsx:60,62`, contrast with `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:671`

One earlier combined run — the same run fired alongside the anomalous tsc invocation above — showed 1/19 failing (`zimmSizeRefinements` "aria-checked" runtime assertion); reran in isolation and combined again, both green. Same conclusion: not reproducible, not reported as a defect.

**What I tried to falsify:** Re-ran `tsc --noEmit` and the vitest suite multiple times after each anomaly, in isolation and combined, specifically to distinguish a real defect from noise — both anomalies vanished on every subsequent run (this session is one of six parallel review agents against a shared, symlinked `node_modules`; my best explanation is resource/process contention from running tsc and vitest concurrently, not a code defect, but I could not instrument the environment enough to prove the mechanism). Traced the full data chain by hand (`activeRefinements` → `refinementFacetGroups` → `ZimmAccordion` → `ZimmCheckboxRefinements`/`ZimmSizeRefinements`) against the actual `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` type definitions for `undefined`, empty-array, and nested-value shapes rather than assuming behavior. } & ({ role?: never; ariaChecked?: never } | { role: 'checkbox' | 'radio'; ariaChecked: boolean }); // `aria-checked` is a selectable control that never exposes what it is set to. // union so the role and its state cannot be supplied apart: a `role="checkbox"` with no // button and never conveys whether it is currently applied. **Verdict: request changes — this can't be approved as it stands.** Two separate things each individually block it, and there are three real logic bugs on top of those. Full findings are logged in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-847/review-pr117.md` as I've gone; one of zm-tester's six angles (live browser check) is still finishing, but nothing left in it changes this verdict — it's just confirming a couple of secondary visual questions.

### The two things that block it on their own

**1. It can't even merge right now.** GitHub shows `mergeable: CONFLICTING`. Why: this branch was cut 41 commits ago and never rebased onto `develop` since — it's not a content problem, it's just stale. Fix: rebase/merge `develop` in before anything else, then re-diff, because some of what I'm about to tell you could shift once that happens.

**2. This PR does about twice the work its own ticket describes, and the extra half belongs to a ticket that's explicitly Blocked.** SFCC-847's own Jira text draws the line for you: it owns the accordion shell and the CLEAR/APPLY *buttons*, full stop — everything else (facet checkboxes/size chips actually working, multi-select logic, applying/clearing filters for real) is explicitly carved out to SFCC-108. This PR builds SFCC-108's part anyway: `zimmCheckboxRefinements`, `zimmSizeRefinements`, and a 153-line `useFilterDrawerState` hook that really does buffer selections and commit them. SFCC-108 is currently **Blocked**, waiting on SFCC-104 (BM facet config) which is still in Code Review — so this code was written against a facet shape that isn't finalized yet. Consequence if this merges as-is: Jira keeps showing SFCC-108 as blocked/not-started while its real functional code already shipped under a different story number, so whatever SFCC-108 was supposed to gate on gets bypassed without anyone deciding to bypass it. Fix: this needs a conversation with whoever owns SFCC-108/847/104 about whether to re-scope the tickets to match reality, not a code change.

*(Bonus, same bucket: SFCC-847 itself is still sitting in "Tech design," and its very last Jira comment — minutes before this PR opened — is Jira's own automation rejecting a readiness check on it. The ticket wasn't supposed to be worked yet.)*

### The Tier 1 problem

`overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` and `zimmTokens.ts` are touched — a real design-token addition (`border.tertiary`), and I checked it against Figma myself, the *value* is correct. But it's a frozen file, the PR's own checklist has "No Tier 1 files modified" sitting unticked, and there's zero review on the PR at all. Fix: needs an actual tier-1-approver sign-off before merge, regardless of whether the value is right.

### Three real bugs, each reproduced (not guessed)

A reviewer wrote small throwaway tests against the actual hook, ran them, watched them fail, then deleted them — this isn't speculation:

- **CLEAR ALL, then APPLY, can silently bump the shopper up a category** (e.g. out of "Dresses" back to "Clothing") because CLEAR blanks the category state instead of restoring what's actually applied.
- **Switching the category radio away and back inside the open drawer, then APPLY, silently wipes a filter the shopper never touched** — the code has a comment claiming this is handled; it isn't, and the repro proves it.
- **Using the browser's Back button while the drawer is open, then APPLY, silently undoes the shopper's own back-navigation** — the state-resync logic only re-runs when the drawer opens/closes, not when the URL changes underneath it.

Fix for all three is in `useFilterDrawerState.ts`/`product-list/index.tsx`'s category-and-refine bookkeeping — a developer call, not a design call.

### The accessibility one worth calling out on its own

Removing a filter chip (probably the single most common action in this whole feature) drops keyboard/screen-reader focus to the very top of the page every time — there's no focus management on any of the three removal sites. That's a direct hit against the ticket's own stated goal of "proper screen-reader announcements."

### Smaller, confirmed stuff (not blocking, worth a cleanup pass)

- A genuinely garbled/scrambled comment in `zimmButton/index.tsx` — three separate reviewers independently tripped over the same corrupted line, so it's real, not a fluke.
- A couple of raw pixel values that should be design tokens (tokens for the exact same values already exist elsewhere in the same file).
- One color token used in the wrong category (text token on a background) — and the hover-state color doesn't even have a correct token to swap to yet, so that one needs a design decision, not just a rename.
- A utility function (`flattenRefinementValues`) was written, tested, and then never actually wired up anywhere.
- Registry docs (`.claude/registry/*.md`) are slightly stale on a couple of rows.
- Facets with zero values still render as a clickable-but-empty accordion panel — no "nothing here" state.

### What I couldn't verify myself

I tried to load the actual filter drawer on this PR's own live preview to eyeball it — every category/PLP page 404s there, traced to a real backend "category not found," unrelated to this PR's code, so I couldn't visually confirm the drawer, the chip layout, or a shared-drawer CSS change that plausibly (not confirmed) affects PDP's mobile drawer too. That last piece is what the still-running sub-agent is chasing down against Storybook instead.

Want the full ranked findings list with file:line, or should I hold for the last sub-agent (should be a few more minutes) before we talk through what actually goes in PR comments?
